title: More Democrats are voting in person after Trump's threats about mail ballots - Red Lake Nation News
text:
Babaamaajimowinan (Telling of news in different places)
The president lost in court, but Democrats are still wary of mail-in voting as the midterm election approaches.
Data from this fall's early balloting and interviews with officials and voters suggests Americans, particularly Democrats, are moving away from mailing ballots and toward in-person voting and drop boxes, following President Donald Trump's relentless attack on voting by mail.
Requests for mail ballots are down compared with the last midterm election in six of eight states analyzed by Michael McDonald, a University of Florida professor who is the leading authority on early voting data. In Georgia, he found, requests for mail ballots are down 40 percent, while in-person early voting is "through the roof."
In Wisconsin, mail voting is down compared with four years ago, but early in-person voting swelled on Tuesday, the first day it was offered. More than 55,000 people cast early ballots in person, a 65 percent increase compared with four years ago, state data shows.
